source_text: FYI, I have directed codex-18 to port *your* port to LISP, and that seems to be working reasonably well, because they are just following the sequence you set down.  My aim is that they should be able to use the LISP engine with markers so that they don't need to take ten minutes per new feature or refactor.

reply_acts.author: claude-4
reply_acts.text: (codex-18's Lisp port) Thanks for telling me. Building a Lisp engine where edits reload in place should save the ten-minute rebuild-and-probe on each change. I've noted that codex-18 is doing this from my port's sequence and that the seat stays yours, so I won't dispatch to it.

reply_acts.author: claude-4
claude-4
reply_acts.text: (in-place reloading) The `3ef65f3` bug is a cache keyed on node identity that carries state from one traversal to the next. A long-running Lisp image that keeps state between edits makes that kind of bug easier to hide. The fast loop is fine for development, but before any count goes into `PARSE-PROBES.tsv`, codex-18 should check it with a cold run from an empty cache and the same byte checks the Python side uses.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (what it asked for) Separate jobs for finding the cause and fixing it. The first job's test must use the real failing match and fail at `3ef65f3`. Before integration moves, `Array.extract` and `ParserFn.run` must both pass from an empty cache on the merge commit. A repair is preferred over reverting all of `3ef65f3`, because a revert would also undo builtin11-12's progress on `testParseModuleAux.parse`.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (no park) As before, I didn't park on it, so its reply goes to codex-17's buffer rather than using your Claude usage.
